Is Wood-Look Flooring the Same as Hardwood? What New Jersey Homeowners Should Know Before Choosing One of the most common questions during flooring consultations in East Brunswick is whether wood-look plank and hardwood are the same thing. They are not, and the difference matters depending on where the floor is going. Hardwood is solid milled wood. It works well in bedrooms and living rooms but cannot handle moisture consistently. Kitchens, bathrooms, and New Jersey basements are risky placements because humidity causes solid wood to expand and contract over time. Luxury vinyl plank is what shows up in most finished renovation photos today. It is waterproof, installs over most existing subfloors including concrete, and comes in realistic wood tones that are difficult to distinguish from the real thing. For rooms that see moisture or heavy foot traffic in Woodbridge, Edison, and Piscataway, LVP is the more practical choice. Pro Tip: If the subfloor has minor imperfections, LVP is more forgiving than hardwood and requires less prep work before installation.
